 COMMON ORDER

The petitioners have sought for quashing of the impugned notices dated 29.08.2025 issued under Section 129 of BNSS, 2023.
2.

It is stated in the impugned notices that the petitioners are accused in Crime No.74 of 2025 registered for the offences under Section 296(b), 115(2), 180(1) and 351(3) of BNS; that the second respondent had made a request to the first respondent to initiate action under Section 129 of BNSS.

The learned Government Advocate would submit that all the petitioners are involved in Crime No.74 of 2025 registered for the offences under Section 296(b), 115(2), 180(1) and 351(3) of BNS.
5.
This Court is of the view that the provisions under Section 129 of BNSS cannot be invoked on mere asking.

Since the petitioners are involved, even according to the respondents, in only one case,
the provisions of Section 129, which actually seeks to obtain security for good behaviour from habitual offenders, cannot be invoked.

sentences.text: Crl.O.P.(MD).Nos.15768 to 15777 of 2025 Clauses (a) to (f) would suggest that the person from whom security for good behaviour is sought for, must have committed the offences habitually.
Clause (g) states that the person must be so desperate and dangerous to render his being at large without security hazardous to the community.
There is no such averment in the impugned notices.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that the impugned notices are totally misconceived and cannot be sustained.
Accordingly, the impugned notices dated 29.08.2025 are quashed and the Criminal Original Petitions are allowed.
